_comment: The variable values every dev Terraform root is applied with. Committed because none of
them is a secret: the state bucket name, a CloudFront-only environment and a tenant UUID
that also seeds local development. Credentials live in Secrets Manager and are never
passed as variables -- see the GITHUB_TOKEN note in the application root.
One file for three roots on purpose. Terraform treats a value for a variable a root does
not declare as a warning, not an error, so `state_bucket` being meaningless to the
foundation root is harmless -- while three files would let the same setting drift between
them. This is the file whose contents go into the TF_VARS_JSON repository secret; the
pipeline writes it into whichever root it is applying.
sender_address is null until a real mailbox is chosen. SES emails a confirmation link to
it and every invitation send fails with MessageRejected until that link is clicked, so a
placeholder here would be worse than nothing: the identity would exist, permanently
unverified, and the failure would surface at the first invitation rather than at apply.
